input: Given /data/team_a.txt and /data/team_b.txt containing member names (one per line, already sorted), use the comm command to find: 1) Members only in Team A (print under 'Only Team A:'). 2) Members only in Team B (print under 'Only Team B:'). 3) Members in both teams (print under 'Both teams:'). Print the count of each group.

transcript.final_response:
Here is the solution using the `comm` command to compare `/data/team_a.txt` and `/data/team_b.txt`:

```bash
only_a=$(comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)
only_b=$(comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)
both=$(comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)

count_a=$(echo "$only_a" | grep -c .)
count_b=$(echo "$only_b" | grep -c .)
count_both=$(echo "$both" | grep -c .)

echo "Only Team A:"
echo "$only_a"
echo "Count: $count_a"
echo ""
echo "Only Team B:"
echo "$only_b"
echo "Count: $count_b"
echo ""
echo "Both teams:"
echo "$both"
echo "Count: $count_both"
```
